How Worried Should We Be About Screen Time During the Pandemic?

The coronavirus pandemic ended the screen time debate: Screens won. We all now find ourselves on our screens for school, for work and for connecting with family and friends during this time of social distancing and increased isolation.

But should we be worried about this excessive screen use right now? Or should we finally get over it and embrace the benefits of our digital devices?

---

In my opinion, we need to step away from the screens some, in social instances, while continuing to embrace them at work. I think IF someone can fill some of time spent in either class or work meaningfully, then they should use screens for this. With the pandemic NOT having totally ended we should mitigate contact with others WITH utilizing screens. WE should still embrace them.
I think we should be careful about the amount of time spent on screens, and I think we should be careful about the content that we consume
 though. While needed for work, using it to substitute fully for all life is bad. We DO need meaningful face to face with loved ones, particularly if they are vaccinated and masked absolutely embrace, love, and see others. Substituting virtual beings and data for life can have quite negative effects, particularly for young and forming minds, for those who are often marginalized and shunned anyway, and for those who have difficulty being alone. We must engage, socially, going out of our way to include, safely, others in real life. It's important to do so. 

It's a sort of delicate balance, involving people while utilizing remote work and schooling can turn out well. It's a balance that I think we should strive for. We need to improve our overall lives BUT we need to utilize screens sometime to do that. If we can minimize long horrid commutes via screens then, we should do this. We should also use that wasted commute time, now saved, to hang out with those we love, spend extra time with children/parents/friends.  Make NEW connections in real life using that time and saved resources. Take advantage, similarly of being able to get educated and improve your job skills via computers. Take up a hobby, involving others if possible. The world can be better and wider doing BOTH work with screens and expanding our social real world.  Lets live life more fully.

Wisely using screens for needed activities but eliminating them from unneeded ones. Shunning social media for news or time fillers and instead opting for real time meetings with friends, go out for coffee or better yet, a walk outside, with close friends. Put the screens away when we aren't at work or school. Open up the world. 
We can do it.
 We can learn, become more, become better. Screens can help if we use them wisely as the tools they are. Avoid using them as crutches though. We can be better and screens can be a part of that improvement.

What Stereotypical Characters Make You Cringe?

What stereotypical characters in books, movies or television shows make you cringe and why? Would you ever not watch or read something because of its offensive portrayal of someone?

---

I can easily say that I cringe notably when I see stereotypical characters in any form of media that effectively portrays people and certain demographics in a negative and offensive way. I cringe from these types of characters because I not only find them lazily written and one-dimensional, but that they are a negative addition to any show, book, or movie, that has consequences to its viewers. Not only do such characters illicit negative responses from other people who find them offensive, but they also perpetuate negative ideas and responses about these character groups in the real world. Many people hold stereotypes towards racial groups, as well as other types of minorities. Stereotypical characters reinforce those stereotypes and thus become a way to perpetuate and even justify negative and stigmatized attitudes towards those character groups. This can lead to said groups being viewed as lesser, even potentially dehumanized. I cannot say that I am willing to accept those characters in any media or content that I consume, given that their presence or implementation are not necessary, or a meaningful addition by the writers or creators of said content. 

For some pieces of media, if the portrayal of a stereotypical character is too offensive or disingenuous and a critically seen part of the content, then I will either avoid that show, book or movie. Seeing such characters are not pleasant for me personally, which is also true of other people, and I don't enjoy engaging with shows that overall make me feel uncomfortable or negative in some way. While there are shows that can make me feel sad or even uncomfortable with what it depicts, in those instances those are intended in either a more thought-provoking way, or respectful manner. I am not referring to those types of cases, and instead refer to how stereotypical characters can feel insulting and unrealistic in the context of a show, movie, and book. They are rarely thought-provoking or meaningful in the context of such media, and could be rewritten to be much more respectful, or even more relevant to struggles of the group. 

Often times, it feels as if creators don't take the time to script stories relatively authentic script about characters or groups, but instead prefer to rely on stereotypes which are easier to implement, and take significantly less time. If I feel that I am not being valued or respected as a viewer watching the show or reading a book, I would prefer to read or view something else. I know there are much more respectful ways for creators to portray characters in their shows, movies, books, etc. than the ones that portray them as no more than stereotypes, and those are a better use of my time. As viewers, writers, consumers, and individuals with other identities who are not well seen in media, we have an obligation to demand better representation, and for others to create as such to reduce stereotypes in society, not reinforce and perpetuate them.

Thus, I preferred to avoid using dating apps, and instead chose to date people without finding first on a dating app. Nevertheless, dating apps, I believe, can give people otherwise more romantic opportunities than they would have otherwise through more traditional means. Dating apps are quite useful and beneficial for many to try out, especially if they struggle to discover and find people to date. Additionally, I do think that dating apps allow for people to more easily meet potential romantic interests for long-term relationships, allowing them to date with less complexity than otherwise. For that reason, I believe dating apps will persist long into the future, being well implemented in how others date as well as other technology that is being refined and improved upon as well.

Like dating apps, technology like Netflix, social media and texting also enables people to connect with each other regarding romantic encounters, especially in the instances where that may be difficult. For dating and romantic relationships, being able to communicate and talk your partner is critical in maintaining trust and a romantic connection, which leads way for a solid relationship or a long-term partnership. Even for short-term relationships, communication via text and social media can improve how positive you view the interactions you have with others. The technology available today has many good benefits to it, in the sense that it allows for us to make connections with others easier and faster, something that can be seen how ubitquitous it is in romantic and non-romantic relationships. Although there are some negatives associated with technology use, specifically when people fail to moderate and balance it well with other aspects of their lives, I believe many would be able to learn and implement how to best use technology in their life. If anything, as time goes on, the technology people use for romantic interactions and dating will get more and more refined, ensuring more positive and favorable outcomes for the user, and potentially ensuring more relationships are made and sustained.
